name: Mecistops
sum: Slender-snouted crocodiles of western and central Africa — two living species recognised on genetic evidence, with Miocene to Pleistocene fossils in East Africa.
wsnote: Adults are typically about 2.5 m long and have reached 4.2 m, weighing 125–325 kg; males are clearly larger than females (genus article, not split by species).
holotype: Living genus — the name-bearing type of the type species is not covered by the sources used.
material: The two living species, plus the fossil M. nkondoensis and other PBDB occurrences from the Miocene to Pleistocene of Uganda, Kenya and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
biology: Slender-snouted crocodiles live in heavily vegetated fresh waters of sub-Saharan Africa and feed mainly on fish, amphibians and crustaceans, occasionally taking small mammals, water snakes, turtles and birds. Females build a mound nest of rotting plants on the bank and lay on average 16 large eggs; incubation is long (often over 110 days) and the incubation temperature sets the sex. The genus was long thought to hold one species; genetic work split it into the West African M. cataphractus and the Central African M. leptorhynchus, which diverged in the Miocene. Both are heavily hunted, have lost ground in several countries and have been little studied.
author: Gray 1844
